newsitem.title: UK: Reunion Mining shares rise on zinc plan.
newsitem.headline: Reunion Mining shares rise on zinc plan.

text.p: Shares in Reunion Mining Plc rose on Friday on the company's plans set out earlier this week for innovative zinc production in Namibia, mining analysts said.
By 1145 GMT the shares were up 10-1/2p at 108p. Trading volume was 411,500 shares.
"It is not the discovery of the ore - rather that they've worked out how to process it," said Socgen mining analyst John Meyer. "This is a stock that is very fortunate indeed."
Earlier this week Reunion said it would carry out a pre-feasability study at the Skorpion zinc deposit in Namibia, following positive results from metallurgical tests.
Studies over the past four months have shown that zinc may be recovered from the Skorpion ore by leaching with sulphuric acid, Reunion said.
The study should be completed in the first quarter of 1997 and Reunion plans to produce 75,000 tonnes of zinc a year.
The operating costs will be low as production will be on site, avoiding the refining and shipping costs associated with concentrate production.
